chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who swore an oath not to speak to a relative of his, he said: It is not binding, so let him speak to the one he swore upon. And he said: Every oath not intended for the face of Allah is not binding, in divorce or otherwise.
ai.seo_question: Is an oath not to speak to a relative binding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that an oath to sever kinship ties is not binding (*laysa bi-shay'*), permitting the individual to fulfill the duty of *silat al-rahim* by breaking the oath. He further generalizes this principle, stating that any oath not intended for the sake of Allah—whether in divorce or other matters—is invalid, emphasizing the Shia jurisprudential focus on the intent (*niyyah*) and purpose behind verbal commitments.
